title: Etale sections are unchanged by extension of a separably closed base field
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $S$ be a $k$-scheme, and let $p:S_K=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ be the projection. For every sheaf of sets $F$ on the small etale site $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], pullback induces a bijection

$$
 \Gamma(S,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(S_K,p^{-1}F).
$$

proof.text: The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(K)\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is flat, since its only local-ring map is $k\to K$ and $K$ is a free $k$-module, and quasi-compact, since $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ is a single point. The projection $p:S_K\to S$ is the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}(K)\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ along the structure morphism $S\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$, so $p$ is flat by the stability of flat morphisms under base change [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and quasi-compact by the stability of quasi-compact morphisms under base change [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change].

For a geometric point $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}(L)\to S$, the geometric fibre of $p$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_k L)$. The field-tensor irreducibility lemma gives that $K\otimes_k L$ has a unique minimal prime, so this fibre is irreducible and therefore connected.
Applying the flat, quasi-compact, connected-geometric-fibre sections comparison to $p$ and $F$ yields the canonical bijection $\Gamma(S,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(S_K,p^{-1}F)$.
